newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares advance, Bombay rallies for sixth day.
newsitem.headline: India shares advance, Bombay rallies for sixth day.

text.p: Indian shares across major bourses ended in positive territory on Tuesday with a spate of buy orders in front-bench stocks pressed by foreign funds helping the market stage a powerful rally, dealers said.
"The market seems to be going up, up and away..we are seeing a bull run," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Participants said hectic buying by foreign funds in stocks such as cement giant ACC, bell-wether Reliance Industries and tobacco conglomerate ITC fuelled a sharp rise in prices.
The rally spurred the Bombay index to a sixth consecutive higher close, a rise of 240 points or over seven percent.
Indian stocks facing a loss of confidence from investors have raced ahead in the New Year boosted by government promises of policy measures to bolster industrial growth and revive sluggish markets.
The sharp rally had led some investors and fence-sitters to jump on the buying bandwagon, analysts said.
Ashish Kacholia, head of research at Prime Broking, said the rally caused a change in investor sentiment, stoking appetites for small stocks.
"Investors are cautious buyers...they are looking at good quality stocks."
Traders said an early bout of cautiousness saw the market fall in mid-session but buying by foreign funds helped the index to close higher.
The index is likely to test resistance near the psychologically important mark of 3,500, they said.
The Bombay 30-share index ended 39.10 points higher at 3,492.26, up from its intra-day low of 3,422.99.
ACC rose 119.0 rupees to 1,471.25 rupees, SBI 12.70 to 266.50, TISCO 5.25 to 194.25, ITC 18.0 to 381.0, BSES 19.20 to 247.0, Tata Power 7.0 to 141.50 and L&T 5.0 to 249.75.
